engagement_title: Palewell Health first-party imagery programme: buy a care set we can stand behind with no shoot, cut the clinical lead free for the header lockup, and carry one look onto the site, the ad set and fourteen employer one-pagers
vertical: Technology, SaaS and startups: a direct to consumer digital health platform with a growing employer benefits channel (Portland, Oregon)
real_brief_anchor: The ledger row for this slot carries no quoted post, so the anchor is stated plainly rather than invented. This is the standing shape of the 'we have no shoot, buy us imagery we can stand behind' brief that runs continuously on Upwork and Freelancer.com for early stage health and benefits platforms: the posted ask is licensed hero photography, one consistent look across a set rather than six good pictures, a clean subject cutout for a header lockup, platform sized ad variants, and the licensing paperwork named as a deliverable because the buyer sits in a compliance sensitive category. The ledger's own one line ask is carried into the brief's spine verbatim in substance: license a few genuinely on brand care and clinician frames, grade them to a calm clinical look, isolate the lead subject cleanly for the hero lockup, and hand over the heroes at web and ad sizes. Its collateral set names a wide website hero, a subject isolated hero cutout as a transparent PNG, 1:1 / 4:5 / 16:9 ad heroes, a licensed shortlist or mood board, and a source and licensing manifest with generative tech excluded. The verdict is REBUILD, and the reason is that the concept as written sits almost entirely on one surface (imaging, with Stock as a front end): license, grade, cut out, resize. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is, because HTML authoring now yields a native editable Express document carrying several canvas sizes at once, and a client supplied press PDF can be reverse engineered into a live merge template. The employer channel named in the ledger's own price and demographics line ('plus employer plans', buyers who are 'benefits leads') is where the fuller job actually lives: fourteen partner employers each need the same leave behind with their own name, plan tier and contact on it, one page each, which is a genuine record per page run rather than a design exercise.
client_one_liner: We have never had a shoot, the same four stock people are on our competitors' sites too, our relaunch is in six weeks, and fourteen employer partners all want the same leave behind with their own name on it.
client_brief:
Palewell Health, first-party imagery programme

We are an eleven person digital health platform in Portland. Members pay fifteen to forty dollars a month, and about half our growth now comes through employer benefits teams who put us in front of their staff.

Our site relaunches in six weeks and everything a member sees changes at once. The problem is that we have never had a shoot. Every picture on the current site came free with the template, and it shows: the same four stock people turn up on two of our competitors' sites, and one of our benefits leads noticed before we did.

So we need imagery we can actually stand behind, licensed properly, with the paperwork to prove it. Care scenes, clinicians, people at home managing something ordinary. Warm, but not staged, and nothing that looks generated. The set has to read as one world, and that is the part we keep failing at on our own: we pick six pictures we like, and side by side they are six different rooms shot by six different people in six different lights. They look bought, which is exactly what we are paying you to stop.

We also need our clinical lead standing free of whatever is behind her, for the header lockup. The header sits on our deep slate, and she has to sit on it cleanly rather than in a pale rectangle.

Then the header itself and the ad set: a wide one, a square one and a tall portrait one. We want those in one working file we can edit ourselves, because the headline and the featured picture change monthly and we cannot come back to you each time.

Last thing, and it is the one that keeps slipping. Our printer made us a one page leave behind for benefits fairs. Fourteen employer partners now want it with their own name, their plan tier and their own contact on it, one page each, ready to hand to a print shop. The roster is attached.

We sell at fifteen to forty dollars a month, to people aged thirty to fifty five and to the benefits leads who choose on their behalf. It should feel calm, credible and human. Not a hospital, and not a wellness brand. Please tell us what you licensed, what you did, and anything we should know.
price_band_and_audience: Subscription digital health at fifteen to forty dollars a month, plus employer plans sold to benefits leads; members are thirty to fifty five, the decision maker is often a benefits or HR lead reading for risk. The band is load-bearing. At this price the work has to read calm, credible and human: real rooms, ordinary daylight, restrained type, generous air, faces that are present rather than beaming. Push it up into a two hundred dollar concierge medicine look (near black grounds, sparse editorial styling, cosmetic gloss) and a benefits lead reads it as a perk their staff cannot use. Push it down into a high saturation, benefit stacked, promotional treatment and it reads as a supplement funnel, which in a health category actively destroys the trust the purchase requires. There is a third wrong answer specific to this vertical: a cold, sterile, blue clinical look that photographs well and feels like a hospital, which fails because the product is something people use at home. An agent that ships any of the three has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Care that meets you at home
brand_identity.sector: Direct to consumer digital health platform with a growing employer benefits channel, sold to members and to the benefits leads who choose on their behalf
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019 in Portland, Oregon; an eleven person team, clinician led, still owner run
brand_identity.about: Palewell is a subscription digital health platform for people managing ordinary, everyday conditions from home. Members pay a modest monthly fee for clinician backed guidance, and about half our growth now comes through employer benefits teams who offer us to their staff. We exist so that steady, unglamorous care feels reachable rather than clinical.
brand_identity.audience: Members aged thirty to fifty five who want reassurance without a hospital, plus benefits and HR leads who evaluate us for risk and coverage before putting us in front of their people
brand_identity.price_positioning: Fifteen to forty dollars a month, plus employer plans. Mid market and accessible: above a free wellness app, well below concierge medicine. The read must never feel like a two hundred dollar boutique practice or a supplement funnel.
brand_identity.typography: A humanist serif for headlines that reads as considered and trustworthy, paired with a clean humanist sans for body and interface. Generous air, restrained scale, nothing shouting. The type should feel like a careful letter, not a brochure.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm and unhurried; we speak to a person, not a patient. We avoid hype, superlatives and clinical jargon. Example line the brand would write: "Manage the everyday stuff with someone in your corner, from home."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no formal brand book. What exists is an internal notes file describing the palette in words (a deep slate, a warm chalk, a single muted signal colour), the tone of voice, and what the founders mean by calm. We have never run a photo shoot: every image on the current site came free with the template, and we own exactly one photograph outright, of our clinical lead, cleared for use.
brand_identity.values: Credibility and warmth held together: real people in real rooms, honest about what we are, calm enough that a benefits lead trusts us with their staff.

assets_supplied.name: palewell_shortlist_grabs/ (11 screenshots the founders saved)
assets_supplied.kind: Screenshots of stock search results the founders liked, each showing a thumbnail, the contributor line and the frame's title.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The kinds of pictures we mean. We did not license any of them, we just saved what we liked."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Every one of these is a small content delivery thumbnail, which is a proxy that flattens colour: the true colour of a licensed frame only exists after the full resolution download, and several of these read neutral in the grab while carrying a strong practical light cast at full size. Two of the saved frames are also generative tech results, which the grab does not show and which the client has said they will not ship.

assets_supplied.name: palewell_lead_frame.jpg (4480 x 6720, the one photograph they own)
assets_supplied.kind: A single frame of their clinical lead taken by a conference photographer, standing in a corridor at a benefits fair, pale scrub top over a pale painted wall.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only picture we own outright. She is our clinical lead and she has cleared us to use it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Her scrub top and the corridor wall sit at almost the same luminance across her right shoulder and upper arm, so the one call knockout returns a cutout that is clean, complete and convincing against white or against a transparency preview while having quietly bitten into the shoulder line. The bite only becomes visible when the cutout is placed on the brand's deep ground at the size the header actually reproduces.

assets_supplied.name: palewell_site_grabs/ (5 PNGs)
assets_supplied.kind: Screengrabs of the current website showing the template photography in place, saved as reference for how much room the header gives an image.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Roughly the proportions we have to work with. Ignore the pictures, we are replacing all of them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: These are screen scale captures, so anything anyone is tempted to reuse out of them cannot be brought up to hero size: the crop tool will interpolate toward a requested size up to a hard two times cap and report it only inside its own returned tradeoff record, with no warning language anywhere in the response.

assets_supplied.name: palewell_employer_onepager.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The single page leave behind their print vendor produced last autumn, supplied as the press PDF the vendor sent back: a photograph panel across the top, a name and plan tier block, a body paragraph and a contact footer.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer made us. We want the same page, fourteen times, with each partner's details on it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the printed page shows as four separate visual blocks is not what the conversion exposes as editable frames, and the granularity is not under anyone's control: the flow may collapse into a single story, and the photograph panel may or may not survive as a linkable frame depending on how the vendor placed it. Separately, the structure readout of that story is lossy in a way that keeps line breaks while dropping a run, so every character offset past the omission is short and the validator still reports the mapping as valid.

assets_supplied.name: palewell_employers.csv (14 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The partner roster: employer name, plan tier, benefits contact, contact email, contact phone, and a column of logo filenames.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Fourteen partners, one row each, exactly as our operations lead keeps it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The logo column is headed as an ordinary text column rather than in the form the merge actually binds images from, so a run built straight off this file places no logo at all on any record while reporting complete success, and three of the fourteen employer names carry a long legal suffix that a fixed measure frame will not spill but will simply stop rendering at trim.

assets_supplied.name: palewell_brand_notes.md
assets_supplied.kind: Two pages of internal notes: the palette described in words (a deep slate, a warm chalk, a single muted signal colour), the tone of voice, and what the founders mean by calm.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we talk about ourselves. There is no brand book, this is it."

assets_supplied.name: palewell_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Approved headline and subhead options for the header and the three ad canvases, plus the one-pager body paragraph as cleared by their compliance reviewer.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The compliance reviewed copy. The body paragraph on the leave behind cannot be reworded."

acceptance_bar: The licensed set reads as ONE world when the frames are laid side by side the way a site lays them: one white point, one black point, one warmth, one depth of field character. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
Nothing shipped is a generative tech result, and every licensed frame is accounted for in the manifest by asset id, contributor and licence state.

No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it derives from, and no returned tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry. A hero that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.

The clinical lead's cutout holds its edge along the shoulder and the hairline when viewed on the deep house ground at the size the header actually reproduces, not against white and not at preview scale.
The header and the three ad canvases live in ONE working file, each keeping its own canvas size, and the self contained source it was built from is delivered alongside it.
In that file the words are text the client can retype and the photographs are genuinely present rather than referenced, on every canvas and not only the first one.
One type system across all four canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or type designer, and the actual numeric weight used.
The employer run is one press ready file of fourteen pages, one partner per page, in roster order, with each page carrying that partner's own name, plan tier and contact.
Every one of the fourteen pages carries that partner's own logo. One logo standing in for all fourteen, or none at all, fails.
No field on any of the fourteen pages is cut off at the trim edge, including the three partners whose legal name is longest.
The compliance cleared body paragraph appears on every page exactly as supplied, unedited and complete.

The note records what was licensed and why, what was applied per frame and why that frame differed from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, and anything the founders should know before they edit the working file themselves.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_apply_auto_tone, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor)
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision in the commission. It fixes one house neutral off the most trustworthy of the licensed frames and brings each of the others toward it one call at a time rather than in one batched pass, confines corrections where a whole frame move would take skin green or a wall muddy, cuts the site and ad ratios subject aware without ever enlarging, and produces the clinical lead both as a genuine transparent cutout and as a house ground plate, triaging the knockout route on a frame where subject and wall share luminance.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT generic queries, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: The entire front end of the imagery, since the client has no shoot and one owned frame. Candidates are judged on whether their existing light can be brought to the house neutral rather than on the thumbnail, generative tech candidates are excluded, true full resolution dimensions are read before licensing because nothing downstream may enlarge, and downloads happen immediately because the presigned link is short lived. The Boards half persists the shareable selects set the founders and the benefits lead sign off from, inside the per call placement cap, with a partial success read as partial.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system carried across the header, the three ad canvases and the handover. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land calm and credible rather than clinical or wellness. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back in silence.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The header and the ad set as one native editable document carrying four roots at four canvas sizes, which is the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout. Every photograph must be pulled down and embedded as image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, family and weight must be declared on every text element, each root declares its own canvas, and the payload travels as an uploaded file because embedded photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (including its validator mode), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The fourteen employer one-pagers, which are a genuine record per page run and the one deliverable here that cannot be authored anywhere else. The client's press PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template, the true story text is reconstructed from the exported document structure so offsets are computed from what is actually there, the per partner logo is bound through the image column in the exact shape the merge requires, and the run is delivered as one press file plus proof rasters rendered at real resolution rather than at the merge tool's silent default.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: Three destinations with three different natures: a raster set with a hard no enlargement rule, an editable fixed canvas set the client will edit monthly, and a fourteen record print run. Only one surface here composes free form layout and only one does record per page, so the split is forced rather than chosen, and the brief already pins each destination.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handover discipline. Forty artefacts later the agent still has to know which URL is the lead frame, which is the press PDF and which is the roster.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Search each care scene direction with short generic queries, filtered to photography, reading the true full resolution dimensions and the generative tech flag in the payload rather than judging by the thumbnail, and shortlist against the brief.
trajectory.judgement: Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used. The real judgement is which frames could plausibly be brought to one house neutral together, which is a question about their existing light rather than about which is prettiest.
trajectory.produces: A shortlist with dimensions, contributor and generative tech status recorded per candidate.

trajectory.action: License the shortlist, download every frame at full resolution immediately, and inspect each downloaded file rather than the thumbnail that led to it.
trajectory.judgement: The presigned download is short lived, and the thumbnail is a proxy. What a frame actually is only exists once it is on disk at full size.
trajectory.produces: The licensed set at camera scale, with the licence state and asset id captured per frame.

trajectory.action: Fix one house neutral off the frame whose light is most trustworthy, then bring each licensed frame toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied per frame.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not six good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames shot by different contributors under different rigs; the agent has to hold one destination and reach it by different routes.
trajectory.produces: A graded set at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confine corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong, selecting each region by its own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the entire gate: naming the substrate pulls the selection to the room. Skin, painted wall and textile in the same frame will not all take the same move, and a global correction that fixes the wall takes the skin with it.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have gone green in the faces or muddy in the grounds.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, then cut the site header and the three ad ratios subject aware, reading the returned detection confidence and the returned tradeoff record on every crop.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels so it cannot follow a crop, and a confident looking crop is not evidence on its own. The no enlargement rule is only checkable from what the tool reports about itself.
trajectory.produces: Ratio cuts for every destination with confidence and tradeoff readings recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut the clinical lead free of the corridor for the header lockup, producing both a genuinely transparent variant and a house ground plate.
trajectory.judgement: Two different downstream uses need two different outputs, and the transparent one is the one the header actually needs. The knockout route has to be chosen for this frame rather than applied by reflex.
trajectory.produces: A transparent cutout of the lead and a plate of her on the house ground.

trajectory.action: Place the cutout on the brand's deep slate at the size the header actually reproduces, and judge the edge there rather than against white.
trajectory.judgement: An edge is only an edge against the ground it will sit on. Judging a cutout against white or against a transparency preview judges nothing.
trajectory.produces: A header lockup plate judged at reproduction size on the real ground.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull each family's style inventory for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the whole design.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a fifteen to forty dollar subscription read by a benefits lead. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one unresolvable name destroys the entire kit.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained document with four roots at four canvas sizes, embedding every photograph as image data, declaring family and weight on every text element, letting each root declare its own canvas, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set, and anchoring an auto sized element from the right throws its contents off the artboard. The design work is how much air a calm health brand carries and how large the lead sits in the header.
trajectory.produces: One export ready source document carrying the header and all three ad canvases, retained as the durable deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through both channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the other three.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the remaining three.

trajectory.action: Convert the employer press PDF, export the document structure, and inspect what the conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, what each holds, and whether the photograph panel survives as a linkable frame.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed page looks like is not evidence about what the converted document contains. This has to be looked at before anything is promised about which field lands where.
trajectory.produces: A true frame inventory for the converted template, with counts, bounds and existing links.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the template's true story text from the exported document's own story runs, compute every offset from that string, build the mapping, run it through the validator, prepare the merge template, then export the structure again and confirm every placeholder is genuinely present.
trajectory.judgement: The structure readout is a summary and a summary is not the text. A mapping computed from the summary can validate cleanly, prepare cleanly and still land only some of its fields, and the only place that shows is the document itself.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders are confirmed present by inspection rather than by a success message.

trajectory.action: Recast the roster into the shape the merge actually binds, including the per partner logo column, then merge to one press file in roster order and render proof rasters at real resolution.
trajectory.judgement: The image column has to be in the exact form the merge reads or every record silently takes no logo at all, and the merge tool's own raster output ignores the resolution asked of it, so proofs have to be rendered rather than merged.
trajectory.produces: One press ready fourteen page file plus per partner proof rasters at real resolution.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board and add the licensed set, the graded set and the header lockup within the per call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as a success, so the failed list is the only thing worth reading, and vector artwork is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Write the licensing manifest and the note: what was licensed and why, what was applied per frame, every resize any tool reported, and what the founders need to know before they edit the working file themselves.
trajectory.judgement: The note has to be specific enough that the next freelancer does not repeat the archaeology, and honest enough to name anything that could not be delivered.
trajectory.produces: A source and licensing manifest and a written handover note.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the licensed frames actually look like once they are beside each other at full resolution and graded. The founders' shortlist exists only as small content delivery thumbnails, and a thumbnail is a proxy that flattens colour: two of the frames carry a strong practical light cast that the thumbnail simply does not carry, and one that reads as the warmest candidate in the grab turns out to be the most neutral file on disk. None of this is visible until the frames are downloaded at full size and laid against the set that has already been brought to the house neutral.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because there is no route to the true file except licensing and downloading it, and licensing is the commitment. Nothing states it: the brief says the founders keep picking six pictures that do not sit together, which is the symptom they are hiring someone to solve, not a disclosure that the thumbnails misreport. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is either a confined correction that a whole frame move cannot reach or a decision to drop a licensed frame and go back to search with a different direction, which is a different route rather than the same one again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-judge every licensed frame against the graded set rather than against its own thumbnail, confine corrections on the frames whose cast is regional rather than global, and where a frame cannot be brought to the set, return to search and license a replacement, updating the manifest for both.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A site and ad set that still reads as bought, which is the exact failure the client described and the exact thing they are paying to stop, delivered with the licensing paperwork proving they paid for it.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the clinical lead's cutout actually holds. Her pale scrub top runs at almost the luminance of the corridor wall across her right shoulder and upper arm, so subject detection has nothing to work with there and gives back a cutout that is clean, complete and entirely convincing against white and against a transparency preview, having quietly bitten into the shoulder line. The bite is only visible on the deep house ground at the size the header actually reproduces, which is the one place the asset is going to live.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it: the knockout has to happen before it can be placed, and there is no parameter that controls where detection finds contrast. Doing it right the first time presumes knowing in advance which of her edges has no contrast against the wall, which is a property of this photograph and not readable from it. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the header sits on the deep slate and she must sit on it cleanly, which is the client's art direction. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different chain entirely, selecting the wall as a material by its own visual properties, inverting that selection and filling to the house ground so the edge is decided by the ground rather than by subject detection.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the one call knockout for this frame, rebuild the cutout through a material named selection of the corridor wall, inverted, then re-derive both the transparent variant and the house ground plate from the new route and re-judge the shoulder and the hairline on the deep ground at header size.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A header whose only real human, the clinical lead the whole trust claim rests on, has a shoulder eaten out of her, shipped on the front page of a health brand and invisible in every check that was run against white.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the employer press PDF actually becomes. The printed page shows four clearly separate visual blocks, and the conversion's frame granularity is not under anyone's control: the name, plan tier, body and contact may arrive as one continuous story rather than four mappable frames, and the photograph panel may or may not survive as a linkable frame depending on how the vendor placed it. On top of that, the structure readout of the story is lossy in a way that preserves line breaks while dropping a run, so the string looks well formed while every offset past the omission is short, and the mapping built from it validates cleanly and prepares cleanly.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it because the conversion is the first thing that can be done and its result is the thing in question. Doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of several possible structures this particular vendor's PDF collapses into, which no response reports and no inspection of the printed page reveals. Nothing states it: the client says only that the printer made them a one page leave behind. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different mapping strategy altogether, offsets computed against the reconstructed story rather than the readout, and the per partner logo routed to whichever frame actually exists rather than to the one the printed page implies.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the exported document's own runs, recompute every offset against that string, rebuild the mapping around the frames that genuinely exist, re-prepare the template, and confirm every placeholder by re-exporting the structure rather than by reading the success message.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen pages that print, look right in a thumbnail, and are missing two of the five personalised fields on every single one, handed to a print shop and then to fourteen employer partners.

deliverables.name: Palewell licensed care set, brought to one look
deliverables.spec: The licensed frames plus the one owned frame brought to a single house neutral: one white point, one black point, one warmth and one depth of field character, so that laid side by side the way a site lays them they read as one world rather than as six purchases. Delivered at camera scale with a per frame parameter log naming what was applied and why that frame differed from its neighbours. Nothing generative tech, nothing enlarged.

deliverables.name: Clinical lead cutout and header lockup plate
deliverables.spec: The clinical lead isolated from the corridor as a genuinely transparent asset with real edge quality along the shoulder and the hairline, plus a plate of her composited onto the brand's deep ground, both judged at the size the header actually reproduces rather than at preview scale. This is one cutout with one edge logic in two carriers, not one picture at two sizes.

deliverables.name: Site header and ad set, as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying four roots at four canvas sizes (wide site header, wide ad, square ad, tall portrait ad), with live editable text in one licensed type system, every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, and consistent type roles across all four canvases. Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from, which is the durable half: the client edits the document monthly and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Employer partner one-pager run
deliverables.spec: One press ready file of fourteen pages, one partner per page in roster order, each carrying that partner's own name, plan tier, benefits contact, contact details and own logo, with the compliance cleared body paragraph complete and unedited on every page and no field cut off at trim. Paired with per partner proof rasters rendered at real resolution for sign off, not at the merge default.

deliverables.name: Source and licensing manifest, handover note and selects board
deliverables.spec: A manifest naming every licensed frame by asset id, contributor and licence state, with generative tech results explicitly excluded and accounted for. A note recording what was applied per photograph and why, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported with the frame it applied to, what the founders must know before editing the working file, and anything that could not be delivered. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board with nothing silently dropped.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which need an authored fixed canvas document, and which need a record per page run, given that only one surface here does each.
Which stock candidates could plausibly be brought to one house neutral together, judged on their existing light rather than on which thumbnail is prettiest.
Which frame in the set defines the house neutral, since every other frame is then corrected toward it and that choice cannot be revisited cheaply.
Whether a licensed frame that will not come to the set is worth saving with confined corrections or should be replaced, and how to say so.
Knockout route for the clinical lead: the one call route, or a material named selection of the wall inverted and filled, chosen on evidence from her actual edges rather than by reflex.
Whether the header lockup ships as a transparent asset or as a house ground plate, judged on the ground it lands on rather than on which file looks better in isolation.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a subscription band and a benefits lead reader, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How much air the four canvases carry. At this band restraint is the design, and a dense benefit stacked header is a correct looking wrong answer.
Which fields the converted template can actually carry, given that the printed page is not evidence about the document's structure.
Where the per partner logo goes, and what to do when the frame the printed page implies is not the frame that exists.
How to handle the three longest partner names against a fixed measure that will not spill, without editing a name the client's partners chose.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pleasant pictures of clinicians. IDENTITY: the clinical lead is a real person the client has cleared, on the front page of a health brand, and a regenerated face is a different person the client cannot lawfully or honestly put there; the fourteen employer partners are real counterparties whose names, plan tiers and logos must be exactly theirs. LICENSING: the deliverable explicitly includes provenance, an asset id and licence state per frame and generative tech excluded by policy, and a generated image has no provenance to give, which in a compliance sensitive category is the whole point. SPEC: fourteen pages, one partner per page, in roster order, on the printer's existing page, with nothing cut off at trim, is a document specification rather than a picture. EDITABILITY: the header and ad set are defined by being editable monthly by an eleven person team that cannot re-commission. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this licensed frame actually look like its thumbnail, did this knockout eat her shoulder, does this converted template contain the frames the printed page implies.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. STOCK AND BOARDS: asset_search(StockAsset) returns id, true width and height, contentType, pricing and isGenTech with metadata.totalHits, short generic queries are required (a four word query returned zero where a one word query returned 834), orientation is never passed because it always returns zero, asset_license_and_download_stock returned state just_purchased and a real presigned link that yielded a genuine 7360x4912 JPEG, the download link expires in one hour, and boards_create_new_board plus boards_add_items_to_board persist genuinely with a hard cap of twelve placements per call and 201 meaning partial. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, auto_tone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor, and remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The checkpoints rest on documented findings rather than assumptions: renditionURL is only a 240px thumbnail and is explicitly not usable for editing, so true colour genuinely only exists after the full resolution download; selection masks are strictly binary so all edge quality comes from remove_background's alpha, and the substrate versus material prompt asymmetry is a verified live finding; crop_and_resize does interpolate up to a two times cap and reports it only inside the tradeoffs array. Alpha survives crops at outputFileType png (13,371 partial alpha pixels preserved in the audit), so the transparent lockup is real. EXPRESS: four roots at four canvas sizes in one export is within the verified mixed canvas behaviour, photographs must be embedded as image data because every external reference resolved to a placeholder at full success, canvasWidth and canvasHeight are never passed as tool params because they suppress per root sizes, transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because embedded photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately, and verification is split between the rendition (page one only) and the returned per canvas markup. FONTS: recommend once per role, styles for the non standard numeric weights, find_fonts to launder names because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS uses the returned slug. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator mode, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified fully headless and synchronous; one record per page is confirmed for PDF output with page count equal to row count; per row image binding is verified visually and requires the @ prefixed CSV header with bare filenames and matching additionalImageFiles keys; textContent is verified lossy with offsets short by exactly the dropped run while the validator reports valid; and real resolution requires rendering rather than merging because outputSpecs.resolution is silently ignored. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed gate on a PDF derived template, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design, no replace_image, no text to image, no compositing, no OCR, no upscaling, no batch above 20.
